h1: Tanzeno Hotel Nong Khai — a spacious boutique stay that gives you more room than the price suggests
intro: If you drive or take the train into Nong Khai and want a clean, spacious room with easy parking at a price you don't have to think twice about, Tanzeno Hotel is the name that comes up most often in this bracket. It's a newer 6-storey building, opened in 2019, that deliberately made its rooms larger than average for the price — comfy beds, strong air conditioning, breakfast included and free bikes to borrow. It sits in the city near the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge, just a few minutes' drive from the border and the river. From approx. THB 1,150/night.

body.html: Tanzeno Hotel opened in 2019 on Mitraphap Road, in the Mi Chai sub-district of Mueang Nong Khai. It's a newer 6-storey building of around 76 rooms, pitched at travellers who want a good room at a sensible price. The thing reviewers agree on most is that the rooms are larger than you'd expect for the money — both the bedroom and the bathroom give you comfortable space, without the cramped feel of many budget hotels.

Room types run from Standard Twin and Standard Double up to a Family Room for larger groups. Rooms are done in warm tones with comfortable beds, strong cold air conditioning, reliable hot water and a stable Wi-Fi connection. To be fair, this is a hotel now into its fifth or sixth year — the white leather furniture in some rooms is starting to show wear, and the TV channel selection is limited. In some rooms the wet/dry separation in the bathroom isn't complete, and there are no in-room coffee facilities, so if you need a morning coffee, bring your own.
"The room was really spacious for the price, the bed was comfortable and the air-con was nice and cold — and parking was easy and roomy. Honestly better value than what we paid."

Something self-drivers love here is the large, easy parking, which isn't common at a city-centre hotel. There's an on-site restaurant, room service and laundry. Breakfast is included in many packages, skewing Asian with some English-breakfast options — most guests find it filling and satisfying, though some reviews note the variety could be wider. Another touch people appreciate is the free bikes to borrow, ideal for a ride around town or out to the river on a nice day.

Be clear about the location. Tanzeno sits in the Mitraphap Road part of the city, close to the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge and the border crossing, which makes getting in and out of Laos very easy. But the hotel itself isn't on the Mekong riverfront or by Tha Sadet Market — those are about a 10-minute drive away. If you plan to sit by the river or wander the market every evening, you'll need a ride or a bike. The area around the hotel is fairly quiet, with few bars or restaurants nearby — great for a peaceful stay, but less appealing if you want to step out straight into the action.

Honestly, Tanzeno Hotel suits people driving into Nong Khai or using it as a base to cross into Vientiane. You get a spacious, clean room, a comfy bed, easy parking and breakfast at genuinely good value. A score of 9.0 from 55 Trip.com reviews and a TripAdvisor rating of 4.2, ranked around #5 of 18 Nong Khai hotels, show most guests come away happy. The trade-offs to accept are that it's an ageing property with some tired touches, and the location isn't on the river — if you can live with those two things, it's one of the best-value picks in town.

A tip from reading the reviews: ask for a higher floor for quiet and a more open view, and if you're travelling as a group or family, the Family Room is better value than booking two separate rooms. Borrowing the hotel's bikes for an evening ride along the Mekong is, for many guests, the most Nong Khai thing you can do here. And if you're crossing into Vientiane, the hotel's spot near the Friendship Bridge saves real time in the morning.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Tanzeno Hotel Nong Khai

faq.q: Where is Tanzeno Hotel Nong Khai and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's on Mitraphap Road, Mi Chai sub-district, Mueang Nong Khai, in the city near the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge and the border crossing (about a 5-minute drive). It's around a 10-minute drive from Tha Sadet Market and the Mekong riverfront, and roughly 30 minutes to cross into Vientiane via the Friendship Bridge. There's large free parking, ideal for self-drivers.

faq.q: How much does Tanzeno Hotel cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Rates start at around THB 1,150/night for a Standard Twin. Standard Double and Standard King rooms run about THB 1,250–1,450, and the Family Room for larger groups is around THB 1,850. All rooms are notably spacious; prices vary by date and package, so always compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Are the rooms at Tanzeno Hotel really spacious, and who is it best for?
faq.a: Rooms here are larger than average for the price, both bedroom and bathroom — the feature reviewers mention most. It's best for self-drivers exploring Nong Khai, families, and anyone using it as a base to cross into Vientiane. It's about space and value rather than design or river views.

faq.q: Does Tanzeno Hotel have a swimming pool and breakfast?
faq.a: There's no swimming pool. But there is an on-site restaurant, room service, and breakfast included in many packages, skewing Asian with some English-breakfast options — most guests find it filling. There are also free bikes to borrow for rides around town.

faq.q: Is Tanzeno Hotel on the Mekong riverfront?
faq.a: No, it's not on the river. The hotel is on the Mitraphap Road side of the city, closer to the Friendship Bridge than to the Mekong. To reach the riverfront or Tha Sadet Market, it's about a 10-minute drive or bike ride. If staying right on the water matters to you, look at a riverside stay in this same series.

faq.q: Is Tanzeno Hotel good for crossing into Vientiane?
faq.a: Very much so. Its spot near the Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge makes an early-morning border crossing easy and time-saving. The large parking lets you leave a car while you head into Laos, and many guests use it as a base before and after crossing to Vientiane.
